item.content:encoded:
The Fiji Bati has named a strong 40-member extended squad for the 2026 Rugby League World Cup, featuring NRL stars Viliame Kikau, Apisai Koroisau, Jahream Bula and Jacob Saifiti alongside a number of Super League players.

Wests Tigers are strongly represented through Bula, Sunia Turuva, Koroisau and the Fainu brothers Latu, Samuela and Sione, while Josese Lanyon has also been part of the Tigers system.

Canterbury-Bankstown Bulldogs powerhouse Kikau is also included, while Newcastle Knights prop Saifiti adds further experience to the forward pack.

Five players currently playing in the Super League have been selected, with Maika Sivo representing Leeds Rhinos, Semi Valemei and Jason Qareqare playing for Castleford Tigers, Waqa Blake with Bradford Bulls and Taane Milne with Huddersfield Giants.

The extended squad also includes Jethro Rinakama, Joseph Litidamu, Mikaele Senibua, Brandon Wakeham, Kurt Donoghoe, Caleb Navale, Kitione Kautoga, Solomone Saukuru, Cyrus Stanley, Elijah Keung, Michael Waqa and Emosi Ravosai.

Jordan Miller, Bayleigh Benty-Hape, Ronald Philitoga, Melikiseteki Nacaginimasei, Jordan Leiu, Kylan Mafoa, Jope Rauqe, Terrell Kalo Kalo, Jimmy Ngutlik, Brenden Naicori, Senivalati Vunibola, Masake Kurukitoga and Huanga Tokona have also been selected.

Former Salford Red Devils, Leigh Leopards and Featherstone Rovers forward Ben Nakubuwai, who is now playing in Queensland's state competition, is also part of the squad.

The squad is expected to be trimmed before the World Cup kicks off next month, where Fiji is pooled with Australia, New Zealand and the Cook Islands.

item.title: George Bower starts again for All Blacks against Springboks
item.description: Prop George Bower, who has links to Fiji, has been named for the second week in a row in the starting All Blacks lineup to take on the Springboks in the third Test of Rugby's Greatest Rivalry in Johannesburg this Sunday. Bower joins Asafo Aumua and Tyrel Lomax in the front row.
item.content:encoded:
Prop George Bower, who has links to Fiji, has been named for the second week in a row in the starting All Blacks lineup to take on the Springboks in the third Test of Rugby's Greatest Rivalry in Johannesburg this Sunday.

Bower joins Asafo Aumua and Tyrel Lomax in the front row.

Tupou Vaa'i, who will play his 50th Test, partners Sam Darry at lock.

Peter Lakai starts at blindside flanker, Luke Jacobson at openside and captain Ardie Savea at No. 8.

Cam Roigard and Ruben Love form the halves combination.

The back three features Damian McKenzie, Will Jordan and Leroy Carter, while Jordie Barrett and Quinn Tupaea are in the midfield.

The forward reserves are Samisoni Taukei'aho, Xavier Numia, Fletcher Newell, Fabian Holland and Wallace Sititi.

Kyle Preston, Anton Lienert-Brown and Josh Moorby are the backline reserves.

This is the ninth time in 13 Test series between New Zealand and South Africa that the series has been tied at one-all heading into the third Test.

The All Blacks have played twice previously at FNB Stadium, winning 29-22 in 2010 and 32-16 in 2012.

As well as Vaa'i playing his 50th Test, McKenzie will play his 80th Test, Jordan his 60th, Newell his 40th and Jacobson his 30th.

With his 33rd Test try last week, Savea took the total number of Test tries scored by the Savea brothers to a world record 79 for siblings. Julian Savea scored 46 Test tries.

They surpassed the Barrett brothers' mark of 78, with Beauden scoring 45 Test tries, Jordie 26 and Scott seven.

The All Blacks take on the Springboks at 3.10am Sunday at FNB Stadium in Johannesburg.

item.title: Krishna calls on fans to turn up in numbers for 2026 Extra BOG
item.description: Extra Bula FC and Fiji national football team captain Roy Krishna is calling on football fans to turn up in numbers as the 2026 Extra Battle of the Giants kicks off today at 4R Stadium at Govind Park in Ba. Krishna says he is excited about the matches ahead and hopes fans will come out and support all the teams competing in the tournament.
item.content:encoded:
Extra Bula FC and Fiji national football team captain Roy Krishna is calling on football fans to turn up in numbers as the 2026 Extra Battle of the Giants kicks off today at 4R Stadium at Govind Park in Ba.

Krishna says he is excited about the matches ahead and hopes fans will come out and support all the teams competing in the tournament.

He says Bula FC jerseys will also be available during the BOG and is encouraging fans to grab one.

Meanwhile, Dayal’s Steel Ba FC President Praneel Dayal says confidence is high in the Ba camp as they look to make home advantage count and add another trophy to their cabinet.

Dayal says Ba has been preparing for the BOG as part of its regular training programme, and morale is high following the team’s two title wins.

He acknowledges there will always be pressure when Ba plays in front of its home fans but believes the players are mentally prepared to handle it.

He is calling on Ba supporters to fill Four R Stadium at Govind Park and get behind the team.

Dayal says other teams have also prepared well, but Ba will be looking to end its eight-year wait for the BOG title and prove itself against Fiji’s best.

Global Care Suva FC and Blue Gas Navua FC will kick off the tournament at 1pm before Extra Supermarket Labasa FC takes on Nasinu FC at 3pm.

Stratum/PPCL Rewa FC will face Khelvin Engineering Lautoka FC at 5pm, while the official opening ceremony will take place at 7pm.

Hosts Ba FC will then take on Tagimoucia Nadi FC in the feature match at 7.30pm.

item.title: Rawaqa, Ma’afu and Soakai lead Fijian coaching appointments at Drua
item.description: Drua says Rawaqa joins the Drua as Forwards Coach, with Ma’afu taking on the role of Scrum Coach, while Soakai has been appointed Defence Coach. They say Dr Thomas joins as Clinical and Performance Psychologist Coach, with Vasu coming on board as Strength & Conditioning Coach.
item.content:encoded:
Drua says Rawaqa joins the Drua as Forwards Coach, with Ma’afu taking on the role of Scrum Coach, while Soakai has been appointed Defence Coach.

They say Dr Thomas joins as Clinical and Performance Psychologist Coach, with Vasu coming on board as Strength & Conditioning Coach.

The appointments mark an important step in the development of Fijian coaching talent, with Rawaqa, Ma’afu and Vasu emerging through Fiji Rugby’s coaching pathways to take up roles with the Drua.

Drua says the new appointments strengthen a coaching and performance group led by Head Coach Brad Mooar and Senior Assistant Coach Mike Catt, bringing together a blend of Fijian experience, international expertise and specialist knowledge as the club prepares for the seasons ahead.

The inclusion of former Flying Fijians Rawaqa and Ma’afu is particularly significant, reflecting the Drua’s commitment to developing homegrown Fijian talent and creating pathways for local coaches to progress to the highest levels of professional rugby.

Mooar says he was incredibly proud and humbled by the quality of the coaching and performance team assembled for the future of the Drua.

He says the new coaching and performance staff were hungry, curious learners and outstanding practitioners, bringing world-class experience from Test rugby, Rugby World Cups and competitions across both hemispheres.

Mooar also highlighted the importance of developing Fijian coaching talent as a foundational principle for the club.

He says the expanded coaching and performance group gives the Drua a strong combination of local knowledge, international experience and specialist expertise as the club continues to build for the future and strengthen its position at the highest level of professional rugby.
